content.page_title: Multidisciplinary management of chronic heart failure (Section 9.2)
content.level_of_evidence_summary: Emphasizes the importance of optimizing delivery of HF care in addition to medical/device therapies; refers to HFA of ESC position papers and need for specialist HF cardiologists and nurses and detailed curricula for training.

9.2.1_models_of_care_summary.purpose: Reduce hospitalizations and mortality by using multidisciplinary HF management programmes (HF-MPs) to ensure correct investigations, accurate diagnosis, evidence-based therapy, education and suitable follow-up.
evidence: Network meta-analysis of 53 randomized trials (published 2017) concluded disease-management clinics and home visits by nurses reduced all-cause mortality compared to usual care; home visits most effective.
IPD meta-analysis of 20 studies (5,624 patients) concluded self-management interventions in HF improve outcomes despite heterogeneity.
9.2.1_models_of_care_summary.comparative_findings: No single service model is consistently superior. While home visits and HF clinics reduce admissions and mortality, educational programmes used alone do not.
9.2.1_models_of_care_summary.implementation_considerations: HF-MPs should be patient-centred, holistic (manage comorbidities such as arrhythmias, hypertension, diabetes, renal dysfunction, and depression), and adapted to the healthcare system and available resources (infrastructure, facilities, staff, finances).

content.palliative_and_supportive_care: Early integration of palliative and supportive approaches is recommended for many HF patients and should be considered for all patients regardless of stage; patients considered for mechanical circulatory support (MCS) or heart transplantation should receive a palliative care consultation prior to such interventions.
content.cross_references: See section 10.2.4 for protocol regarding palliative consultation before MCS or transplantation.
content.raw_text_excerpt: In order to reduce hospitalizations and mortality, earlier guidelines recommended the use of multidisciplinary HF management programmes (HF-MPs), which enable patients to have the correct investigations, an accurate diagnosis, appropriate evidence-based therapy, education, and suitable follow-up. The optimal implementation of a HF-MP requires a multidisciplinary team that is active along the whole HF trajectory; from onset, through critical events, periods of apparent stability, and its terminal stages. A network meta-analysis including 53 randomized trials published in 2017, concluded that both disease-management clinics and home visits by nurses reduced all-cause mortality compared to usual care; home visits being most effective. An IPD meta-analysis of 20 studies, including 5624 patients, concluded that self-management interventions in HF patients improve outcomes despite heterogeneity in the intensity, content, and the personnel who deliver the interventions. HF-MPs vary in their components and can apply different service models... HF-MPs should be patient-centred and take a holistic approach to the patient rather than focussing solely on HF; management of comorbid conditions, such as arrhythmias, hypertension, diabetes, renal dysfunction, and depression, improve patient well-being and self-management, leading to better outcomes.
